issues.t: Charging unit (ICCU) failure, dead 12V battery and limp mode
issues.sym: The SUV stops charging on home or public AC chargers, a 'Check electric system' warning appears, the 12-volt battery goes flat so the car won't start, or it drops into a reduced-power limp mode. Some owners also see the instrument screen flicker or go black.
issues.why: The Integrated Charging Control Unit (ICCU) charges both the drive battery and the 12-volt battery. A transistor inside it can fail under heavy electrical load and blow a fuse, after which the 12-volt battery is no longer charged. Consumer Reports estimates it affects a small share of Hyundai and Kia E-GMP EVs, and owners report code P1A9096.
issues.next: If you get a warning while driving, pull over somewhere safe and call Kia roadside assistance. Have the dealer read the codes and check for ICCU software campaigns. This is covered by Kia's EV component warranty, so do not pay for it out of pocket on a newer car.

issues.t: High-voltage battery cells can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a problem. Some owners notice they can't charge to full.
issues.why: Some battery cells may have misaligned electrodes inside, which can short and cause a fire whether the SUV is parked or driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-431. Until it is fixed, park outside away from buildings and limit charging to 80 percent. The dealer replaces the high-voltage battery for free.

issues.t: Rear drive unit motor shaft can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Reduced acceleration, a warning light, or a sudden loss of drive power, sometimes with noise from the rear.
issues.why: The motor shaft in the rear gear drive unit may have been welded poorly at the factory and can be damaged.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-115. The dealer replaces the rear gear drive unit for free.

issues.t: Differential gear bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the drive unit, loss of power, or the drive wheels locking up.
issues.why: Bolts inside the gear drive unit (differential) may not have been tightened enough at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-271. The dealer replaces the gear drive unit under the recall.

issues.t: Instrument screen can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's display goes dark while driving, so you can't see your speed or warning lights.
issues.why: A software error in the instrument cluster can make the screen fail. Kia recalled 2024–2025 EV9s in October 2024 and recalled 2026 models for a similar fault in January 2026.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 24V-757 and 26V-046. The fix is a free software update done over the air or at the dealer.

issues.t: Second- and third-row seat bolts may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat may rock, clunk or feel loose.
issues.why: Some second- and third-row seats were built without all their mounting bolts, so they may not hold occupants in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-962. Avoid using a loose seat until the dealer installs any missing bolts for free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not switch off for a child (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag 'off' indicator may not light up when a child or child seat is in the front seat.
issues.why: Wiring for the front passenger occupant sensor may be routed wrongly, so the system may not turn the airbag off for a small occupant.
issues.next: Keep children in the back seat. Check your VIN for recall 26V-545; the dealer replaces the sensor mat and corrects the wiring for free. Owner letters start October 20, 2026.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt may not lock properly (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger belt may not lock for a child seat, or the retractor cover looks loose.
issues.why: A cover on the front passenger seat belt retractor may be loose, which can stop the locking feature from working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-338. The dealer replaces the front passenger seat belt for free.

issues.t: Headliner padding may not protect in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The problem is hidden above the headliner.
issues.why: The impact-absorbing plates in the headliner may not meet the federal head-protection standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-400. The dealer replaces the headliner padding plates for free.

issues.t: Remote parking assist may misjudge stopping distance (recall)
issues.sym: When using Remote Smart Parking Assist from outside the SUV, it may not stop as soon as expected.
issues.why: A software error in the electronic brake system can make the remote parking feature miscalculate stopping distance.
issues.next: Avoid using remote parking near people or objects until fixed. Check your VIN for recall 24V-693; the dealer updates the brake software for free.

issues.t: Home AC charging stops working in cold weather
issues.sym: Level 1 or Level 2 charging stops or won't start, especially in cold weather, while DC fast charging still works.
issues.why: On EV9s built from September 2023 to January 2024, a temperature reading inside the charging unit (ICCU) can drift during AC charging, which can damage the unit. Kia changed the coolant pump logic with a software update (service action SA560).
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether service action SA560 has been done. If AC charging has already stopped working, the ICCU may need replacing under warranty.

issues.t: LED headlight control module needs software update
issues.sym: The LED headlights may not work as designed.
issues.why: Kia released a software update for the LED headlamp control unit (service action SA567), sent over the air or done by the dealer.
issues.next: Accept pending over-the-air updates, or ask the dealer to install SA567.

issues.t: Wireless phone charger behaves erratically
issues.sym: The wireless charging pad may not charge the phone as it should.
issues.why: Kia changed the wireless charger's control logic with a software update (service action SA561).
issues.next: Ask the dealer or install the over-the-air update for SA561.

issues.t: Radio icons don't respond on the touch screen
issues.sym: Tapping the AM, FM or SiriusXM icons on the touch screen does nothing.
issues.why: Kia bulletin ELE303 covers non-responsive radio icons on the AVN 5.0 infotainment system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to apply the infotainment software update.

issues.t: Power seats don't move or remember positions correctly
issues.sym: The power seats may not operate as designed.
issues.why: Kia updated the power seat control module software (service action SA557).
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check whether SA557 has been done.

issues.t: Rear end sways or hops over bumps at highway speed
issues.sym: Over bumps at highway speed the rear of the SUV moves sideways or hops, which feels unsettling.
issues.why: Reported by owners; the cause has not been confirmed. Tires, alignment and rear suspension parts are the usual places to check.
issues.next: Have the dealer road-test the SUV with you, check tire pressures and alignment, and inspect the rear suspension.

issues.t: Charging errors and slow speeds with the NACS port
issues.sym: Charging sessions stop and start with error messages, older CCS public chargers need an adapter, and Tesla Supercharger speeds can be lower than expected.
issues.why: The 2026 EV9 uses the newer NACS (Tesla-style) port. Owners report adapter and compatibility problems and slower charging at some stations.
issues.next: Use only adapters approved by Kia, try a different station, and ask the dealer about charging software updates if errors continue at home.

issues.t: Steering wheel and seat vibration at highway speed
issues.sym: Shaking in the steering wheel, seats and console at roughly 65–80 mph.
issues.why: The cause has not been confirmed. Some owners traced it to tires; others still had it after new tires and alignment.
issues.next: Have the tires road-force balanced and checked for defects. If it continues, document it with the dealer for a warranty repair.

issues.t: Sunroof banging, wind noise or cracked glass
issues.sym: Loud banging or wind noise from the roof at highway speed; in some cases the sunroof glass cracks or water gets in.
issues.why: Owners report sunroof defects and poor sealing; Kia has not published a specific cause.
issues.next: Keep the sunroof closed and have the dealer inspect it under warranty. Watch for water stains on the headliner.

issues.t: Center screen goes black and warning chimes won't stop
issues.sym: The infotainment screen goes black while driving and needs a restart, and warning chimes keep sounding.
issues.why: Owners report software glitches; no specific bulletin has been published.
issues.next: Restart the infotainment system, install any pending over-the-air updates, and report it to the dealer.
